## Requirement

Add a single ValidationRule on Opportunity that blocks any save reducing Amount once StageName is Closed Won, using PRIORVALUE(Amount) guarded against insert, with a named bypass for exempt users/integrations and an error message that states the problem and the fix; scoped to one metadata artefact with no new object, field, or automation.

## Scope

### In scope

- Block any Opportunity save that lowers Amount once StageName = Closed Won; Amount is typed directly on the Opportunity, no Opportunity Products / Line Items roll up into it (Q1).
- Sales-Ops-only correction path via a named Custom Permission carried by a dedicated Permission Set, not a Profile exemption (Q3).
- Deploy the rule active=true using a delta check (Amount < PRIORVALUE(Amount)) so it fires only on a further decrease and does not retroactively re-block the handful of historical violations, which are left as-is (Q5).
- Error message fixed to the Q4 default text, attached to the Amount field, which is on the standard layout(s) in scope (Q4, Q8 default).

### Out of scope

- Cleaning up the historical Closed Won Opportunities whose Amount was already lowered — Q5 explicitly declines any data clean-up; carried as assumption via the delta-check design instead.
- A record-triggered flow or Apex path for Amount — Amount is edited directly and no Opportunity Product / Line Item rollup exists (Q1), so the platform-native validation rule is sufficient.
- Any bypass or contract change for an external system — no ERP, CPQ or billing system writes Amount; only Sales Cloud UI users and the Q6 quarterly Data Loader job, which does not touch Amount (Q7).
- Any change to the Opportunity sharing or field-level-security model — the existing model applies unchanged (Q11 default, assumption A4).
- A new report or dashboard counting blocked saves — save-time control only (Q13 default, assumption A6).

| Lock Opportunity.Amount against a decrease once Closed Won, with a Sales-Ops-only bypass | `fit` | Native ValidationRule with a PRIORVALUE delta check enforces the invariant; the bypass is a native CustomPermission read via $Permission and granted through a PermissionSet. No Apex, no Flow, no callout. Mechanism and bypass-pattern ranking (Custom Permission preferred over Profile/RecordType) per admin/validation-rules (Bypass patterns table, Formula Best Practices) and admin/custom-permissions (Pattern: Admin-Only Bypass in Validation Rules). |

## Assumptions

| Id | Assumption | Because |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `A1` | Amount is visible on the standard Opportunity page layout(s) in the rule's scope, so errorDisplayField=Amount renders next to the field rather than relocating to Top of Page. | Q8 |
| `A2` | The rule's formula references only Amount (Currency) and StageName (Picklist) — no compound fields (address, person name, dependent picklist), which validation rules cannot use as of API 20.0. | Q9 |
| `A3` | No current workaround (report or manual review) catches an Amount decrease after Closed Won today; this rule is a net-new control, not a replacement for an existing safeguard. | Q10 |
| `A4` | No new record-access or field-level-security restriction is in scope; the existing Opportunity sharing and FLS model applies unchanged. | Q11 |
| `A5` | Only internal Sales Cloud (employee) users edit Opportunity Amount; no customer, partner, or contractor portal persona touches this field. | Q12 |
| `A6` | No new report or dashboard is requested alongside the rule; this is a save-time control only. | Q13 |

## Decisions

| Id | Decision | Decision tree | Branch | ADR | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `D1` | Grant the Sales Ops bypass as a Custom Permission (Bypass_Opp_Amount_Lock) carried by a dedicated Permission Set (Opp_Amount_Lock_Bypass), rather than a Profile exemption or a RecordType-scoped exclusion. | — | — | ✔ | standards/decision-trees/automation-selection.md and standards/decision-trees/sharing-selection.md were both checked against README.md's routing table; neither tree routes a validation-rule bypass mechanism (that is a bypass-pattern choice, not an automation or sharing-layer choice). admin/validation-rules' Bypass Patterns table ranks Custom Permission first ('Preferred — granular, auditable') ahead of RecordType scope and marks Profile check 'not recommended'; admin/custom-permissions' Pattern: Admin-Only Bypass in Validation Rules gives the identical two-artefact shape. Q3's answer independently rules out a profile exemption by name, so the requester's instruction and the skill's documented default agree. |
| `D2` | Deploy the validation rule active=true despite existing historical Closed Won Opportunities whose Amount was already lowered, relying on a delta check (Amount < PRIORVALUE(Amount)) rather than an absolute check, so already-violating records are not retroactively re-blocked on unrelated edits. | — | — | ✔ | No decision tree covers 'deploy a validation rule active vs inactive against known-dirty data.' The skill's own Questions-to-Ask row 6 and the PRIORVALUE gotcha establish that a delta-based formula fires only on a further decrease, so a record that is already a historical violation (a fact already true today) does not retrigger the rule on a save that leaves Amount unchanged or raises it; Q5's answer explicitly declines any data clean-up, which an active=false deploy would otherwise force. |

- `D1`
  - Source reference: `skills/admin/validation-rules/SKILL.md`
  - Alternatives rejected: Profile-based exemption ($Profile.Name check); RecordType-scoped exclusion
  - Consequences: The bypass is auditable via a SetupEntityAccess query and revocable per user without touching a profile, at the cost of two artefacts (CustomPermission + PermissionSet) instead of one; the validation-rule checker's VR-REF-02 $Permission resolution depends on the CustomPermission file being present in the same scan tree as the rule.
- `D2`
  - Source reference: `skills/admin/validation-rules/SKILL.md`
  - Alternatives rejected: Deploy active=false pending a data-cleanup project; An absolute check disallowing any Amount below its value at the moment of Closed Won, regardless of edit direction
  - Consequences: The handful of already-violating records remain permanently non-conforming by design; any future edit to Amount on those records that decreases it further is still blocked exactly like any other Closed Won record.

## Milestones

### M1 — Lock Opportunity Amount after Closed Won

Goal: Given a Closed Won Opportunity, when a user without the Bypass_Opp_Amount_Lock custom permission attempts to save a lower Amount, then the save is blocked with the Q4 error message; when a Sales Ops user holding the Opp_Amount_Lock_Bypass permission set makes the same edit, then the save succeeds.
